documents.unit: Office of Information Technology (MyCGU AI guidance)
documents.title: Guidance for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the application of AI to CGU
documents.summary: A short university-wide guidance page that frames AI as unavoidable, lists six guiding principles, and announces a ChatGPT EDU license. It welcomes free AI tools if data privacy policies are followed. It sets no rules for coursework, assessment, disclosure or misconduct and links to other CGU policies instead.
documents.stance_why: The page says the "academic community is welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, as long as they are used in compliance with CGU data privacy policies", which is permission with a condition. It does not hand course decisions to instructors or set any ban, so permit fits better than delegates.

units.why: The opening says "ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic—it could mean missing out", which gives a reason for engaging with AI and frames it as a skill worth having, so it is a professional-skill rationale (P44) rather than a framework statement. It informs and leans toward encouraging use.
units.anchor: ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic—it could mean missing out

units.why: The page states its purpose: "high-level info, policy, and considerations for using AI effectively in teaching, learning and working at CGU". This sets scope and purpose for the institution, so it is an institution-wide framework (P56), not a rule on use.
units.anchor: high-level info, policy, and considerations for using AI effectively in teaching, learning and working
units.frag_end: teaching, learning and working at CGU

units.why: The text acknowledges "the landscape is constantly evolving" and says "thoughtful engagement is the best path forward", which marks the guidance as provisional. That is P54 (revisit regularly) since it concerns change over time, not the framework itself.
units.anchor: while the landscape is constantly evolving, thoughtful engagement is the best path forward

units.why: CGU says its approach to AI is "thoughtful, purposeful, and aligned with the university’s mission to advance knowledge for the public good". This is a statement of institutional principle and purpose, so P56.
units.anchor: our approach to AI is thoughtful, purposeful, and aligned with the university’s mission

units.why: The strategy is described as "balancing innovation with ethical responsibility, and navigating challenges like cost and computing demands". It names ethics and cost as concerns, which fits P53 (ethical concerns) better than P56 because the passage names the concerns themselves.
units.anchor: balancing innovation with ethical responsibility, and navigating challenges like cost and computing demands

units.why: Principle 1 says "People, not technology, must be at the center of our work". It is a principle of the institution-wide framework (P56) with a must modality, addressed to the whole community.
units.anchor: People, not technology, must be at the center of our work

units.why: Principle 2 says the technology "must be easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds to bridge accessibility gaps". This is an equity and access requirement, so P51.
units.anchor: must be easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds to bridge accessibility gaps

units.why: Principle 3 says "Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education". It justifies teaching AI-related literacy as a skill students need, so P44 (AI use as a skill) rather than the generic framework type.
units.anchor: Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education

units.why: Principle 4 says "AI tools should enhance teaching and learning", a recommendation about the purpose of AI use at the institution. It belongs in the framework of principles (P56) with a should modality.
units.anchor: AI tools should enhance teaching and learning

units.why: Principle 5 says "Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process". It is a statement that learning about technology never ends, so it is a principle in the framework (P56), not a rule on use.
units.anchor: Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process

units.why: Principle 6 says "AI research and development must be done responsibly". It governs AI work in research and scholarship, so P62 fits better than P56 or P53 because it is about research conduct.
units.anchor: AI research and development must be done responsibly

units.why: CGU "has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license" for its academic community. This is a university-provided, licensed AI tool, so P17 (sanctioned tool) fits, with the privacy claim coded separately.
units.anchor: Claremont Graduate University has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license
units.policy: CGU provides its academic community with access to a ChatGPT EDU license for research, teaching, and productivity.

units.why: The license "offers enhanced security and privacy protections, ensuring that interactions with AI remain confidential and compliant with CGU policies". This is a data privacy claim about a vetted tool, so P50, not P17 which is about provision.
units.anchor: enhanced security and privacy protections, ensuring that interactions with AI remain confidential

units.why: The community "is welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, as long as they are used in compliance with CGU data privacy policies". It permits tools on a data privacy condition, so P50 (data protection, tool conditions) is chosen over P02, which is about a course or unit default.
units.anchor: welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini

units.why: The page says the listed CGU policies "communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community" and names policies such as the Appropriate Use of Computing Policy and the Policy and Procedures for Violations of Standards of Academic Integrity. This points readers to the institution-level policy framework (P56).
units.anchor: CGU policies communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community

documents.title: AI - Center for Academic & Faculty Excellence
documents.summary: A teaching-center resource page that offers faculty communities, webinars, a curated reading list and one-on-one consultations about AI. It sets no rules for students or instructors and states no default stance. Most of the text is a reference list of articles.
documents.stance_why: The page says CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity" but states no rule for students, no tier and no default, and leaves choices to faculty. With no stance of its own, delegates fits.

units.why: CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity, ethical responsibility, and intellectual ownership". This is a statement of support for faculty learning and using AI, so P63.
units.anchor: supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity

units.why: "Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship" offers a faculty community on AI, which is support for faculty learning (P63).
units.anchor: Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship

units.why: The OIT SharePoint "is designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities and access technology-related resources". It is a resource for learning about AI tools, so P63 over P17 because it is for exploring rather than a sanctioned course tool.
units.anchor: designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities and access technology-related resources

units.why: The webinar archive offers "curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching and deepen your learning", which is faculty development on AI, so P63.
units.anchor: curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching and deepen your learning

units.why: A quoted passage in the resource list says "The task now is to design assessment that incorporates AI-generated text." It recommends redesigning assessment around AI (P35). It is a quotation the page reproduces, not CGU's own rule, so modality is should and the policy is weak.
units.anchor: The task now is to design assessment that incorporates AI-generated text.

units.why: The same quotation says "upon graduation, students will be using this technology in the workplace", a career rationale for engaging with AI, so P44 as a quoted reason.
units.anchor: upon graduation, students will be using this technology in the workplace

units.why: The curated list describes resources on "using text generators for help preparing courses and assessing students", which concerns instructor use of AI for teaching work (P59). It describes a referenced resource and gives no rule, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: using text generators for help preparing courses and assessing students

units.why: The list includes a referenced guide "Guidance on AI Detection and Why We’re Disabling Turnitin’s AI Detector". It points faculty to an argument against relying on detectors (P39), but only as a cited title, not CGU's stated position.
units.anchor: Guidance on AI Detection and Why We’re Disabling Turnitin’s AI Detector

units.why: "CAFE provides personalized guidance on instructional design, teaching challenges, and certificate pathways" offers consultations to faculty, which is support for instructors (P63).
units.anchor: CAFE provides personalized guidance on instructional design, teaching challenges, and certificate pathways

notes: No school or computing-unit AI policy found, per collect file. The CGU Standards of Academic Integrity were not collected (page empty), so misconduct rules are not coded. Linked policies on the MyCGU page were not fetched. Several CAFE units come from quotations and cited titles inside a reference list and are weak policy statements.
